The claim requires explicit restrictions at each responsible semantic boundary, identifying the excluded construct, exclusion rationale, user-visible impact, and phase response. Normally that response must be a diagnostic or conservative incomplete result; temporary approximations, including Lifetime::Dummy, must explicitly disclose a soundness exception instead of implying full Rust semantics. All these requirements remain within the single TODO implementation association in sage_meta::todo: uniform restriction/completeness accounting is not yet enforced at every semantic boundary. This is an explicit cross-cutting implementation gap, not a claimed completed capability.

Its comment explicitly defers acceptance and rejection fixtures for every listed restriction at the encountering phase, with diagnostic, incomplete-result, or documented-approximation behavior matching stated impact. Completing uniform boundary accounting and the corresponding exclusion/reason/impact/response descriptions is the prerequisite for this comprehensive fixture matrix; approximation cases must retain explicit soundness-exception disclosure. The neighboring implementation TODO supplies that prerequisite in the same captured context. The full claim is therefore accounted for as deferred, including rationale and the exception qualification; nothing is relabeled implemented. No helper dependencies are relied on beyond the initial captured fragments. No edits requested to this justified TODO accounting.
